raw_response:
*Speaking as Old Wang, 70, from a village in Quzhou...*

Well, I've been planting cotton on this bit of land for most of my life. Three mu isn't much — my son works in the city now, sends some money home, so we don't depend only on the cotton. But I still work the land. What else would I do at 70? And cotton is what I know. The soil here is decent, not too salty like the lower fields east of us.

This year I'll plant cotton again, the whole 3 mu. No reason to change. Prices were alright last year, and I still have the plastic mulch rolls from the co-op. I'll go with Bt cotton seeds from the agricultural supply store in town — the 国欣 (Guoxin) variety or whatever they have. The old folks used to save seed but nobody does that anymore with these hybrids, it doesn't work the same second year.

For fertilizer, I do what I've always done. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer — one bag of 15-15-15 per mu, that's 50 jin, so about 25 kg. Then at the budding stage in late June I topdress with urea, maybe 15 kg per mu. That works out to around 13-14 kg of nitrogen per mu total. The extension guy came through a few years back saying we over-fertilize, but when I cut back one year the bolls didn't fill as well, so I went back to my way.

Irrigation — I'll pump from the well twice most likely. Once around budding if it's dry, once at boll-forming. Pumping costs money, the electricity meter runs, so I don't do it unless the leaves start to wilt. If the summer rains come good I might only irrigate once.

Pests are the problem every year. Even with Bt seeds the mirid bugs and aphids come. I'll spray insecticide probably 3-4 times through the season. Herbicide once after planting, under the mulch. I hand-weed the rest with my wife — at our age it's slow but we manage on 3 mu.

For plowing, I pay the neighbor with the small tractor, maybe 80 yuan for all 3 mu. Planting I do by hand with the mulch, my wife helps, sometimes my daughter-in-law. Picking in September-October is the hardest — we pick three times through the season, the family comes back from town to help on weekends. If we run short I pay a few day laborers at 100-120 yuan a day.

I expect maybe 250 kg per mu of seed cotton, which gives about 90 kg lint after ginning. Some years better, some years worse. Last year was okay.
